title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: In embedded automotive electronics, you win the contract in the R&D lab, but you earn or lose the cash flow on the SMT line and the semiconductor allocation desk.
epigraph.author: Tier-1 electronics operating maxim

web_blocks.html: SEDEMAC's go-to-market model is overwhelmingly direct B2B OEM co-development rather than retail distribution [7, 13]. In Mobility, engineers embed directly with OEM powertrain teams 18 to 36 months before a vehicle launch to calibrate ISG, EFI, or EV MCU firmware to the specific engine or motor [7]. Once homologated under BS-VI, OBD Stage II-B, or EV safety norms, SEDEMAC ships directly to OEM assembly plants on just-in-time schedules [15]. In Industrial gensets, SEDEMAC combines direct OEM sales (to Kirloskar, Mahindra Powerol, and North American engine/genset makers like Generac) with an aftermarket and panel-builder distributor network for GC-series AMF controllers [8, 13].

On the manufacturing side, SEDEMAC is executing a major capacity expansion centered in Pune and expanding into Tamil Nadu [5]. Its primary 40,000 sq. ft. plant in Chakan, Pune (MF1) has been running above 90% utilization, prompting the build-out of MF3—a 120,000 sq. ft. facility in Chakan (~3x MF1's footprint) that commenced pilot production in Q2 FY27 and is expected to operate around 65–70% utilization post-ramp [5]. A smaller 9,000 sq. ft. unit (MF4) in Chakan is dedicated to electric machines with commercial shipments slated for Q3 FY27, while SEDEMAC also acquired ~13 acres at Shoolagiri (SIPCOT, Tamil Nadu) for MF5 to sit closer to South Indian OEMs [5].

The supply chain's Achilles' heel sits upstream in silicon and printed circuit boards (PCBs) [14]. Over 70% of SEDEMAC's raw material bill is tied to semiconductors and imported electronic components, including PCBs sourced from China and global fabs [14]. During H1 FY27, tighter global semiconductor lead times (exacerbated by AI data-center demand) and PCB inflation squeezed gross margins and forced management to shorten accounts payable days—paying chip vendors faster to lock in allocations—while building inventory buffers [5]. This directly explains why working capital expanded from ~₹135 Cr in March 2026 to ~₹258 Cr by September 2026 [5].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC: Worked ₹100 Revenue-to-Free-Cash-Flow Waterfall (FY26 Audited)
web_blocks.takeaway: Every ₹100 of FY26 revenue yields ₹20.51 in Operating EBITDA and ₹9.83 in accounting PAT, converts into ₹12.10 of operating cash flow (CFO), and finishes at -₹4.44 of Free Cash Flow after ₹16.54 of capacity-expansion capex [1].

web_blocks.title: Unit Economics Reality Check: IP Margins vs. Working-Capital & Capex Intensity
paragraphs: At the gross and EBITDA line, SEDEMAC earns software-like incremental economics on standardized hardware: ₹20.51 EBITDA per ₹100 of revenue in FY26 despite 61% material costs [1, 4].

Below the EBITDA line, however, SEDEMAC behaves like a capital-intensive electronics manufacturer. Between FY25 and H1 FY27, Debtor Days stretched from 24 days (29.7 days baseline) to 46.1 days, Inventory Days hovered at 106–120 days, and FY26 capex of ₹175 Cr pushed Free Cash Flow to -₹47 Cr [1].

book_paragraphs: If you walk into a retail auto-parts market in Pune or Delhi, you will not find SEDEMAC ISG boxes sitting on a shelf next to spark plugs. SEDEMAC is a pure-play B2B engineering partner. In its Mobility business, sales begin 18 to 36 months before a single rupee of revenue is booked. SEDEMAC's application engineers sit alongside an OEM's powertrain team to tune firmware algorithms to the exact inertia, compression ratio, and thermal profile of a new engine or electric motor. Once the vehicle clears BS-VI or OBD Stage II-B homologation with SEDEMAC's ECU inside, the relationship locks in for the multi-year production life of the model. In the Industrial genset segment, that direct OEM model is supplemented by a distributor and panel-builder network that sells GC500 and GC800 AMF controllers into commercial backup power.

Delivering millions of those boxes requires serious physical iron behind the software. SEDEMAC's main 40,000-square-foot plant in Chakan, Pune—called MF1—has been running above 90% capacity utilization. To break that bottleneck, management has embarked on an aggressive footprint build-out: MF3, a 120,000-square-foot Chakan facility roughly three times the size of MF1, entered pilot production in Q2 FY27; MF4, a 9,000-square-foot unit for electric machines, is slated for commercial shipments in Q3 FY27; and SEDEMAC has acquired roughly 13 acres in Shoolagiri, Tamil Nadu for MF5 to put production right next door to its South Indian OEM anchor.

Now let us trace ₹100 of FY26 revenue all the way down to Free Cash Flow so you see the exact unit economics—no guesswork, just audited arithmetic. Out of every ₹100.00 billed in FY26 (₹1,058 crore total), ₹61.00 went out the door for direct materials and components (₹662.11 crore of materials consumed, adjusted for inventory). Another ₹8.19 paid for engineering and factory payroll (₹86.61 crore), and ₹10.31 covered other operating overheads (₹109.03 crore). That leaves ₹20.51 of Operating EBITDA (₹217 crore)—a remarkably healthy margin for an auto-component supplier, proving that proprietary firmware commands real pricing power over commodity hardware.

Keep walking down the waterfall, though, because this is where the electronics reality shows up. Depreciation on automated surface-mount lines and test rigs takes ₹5.95 (₹63 crore), interest takes ₹0.85 (₹9 crore), other income adds ₹0.47 (₹5 crore), and taxes take ₹4.35 (₹46 crore), leaving ₹9.83 of net profit (₹104 crore). Add back depreciation and subtract the working-capital drag—remember, debtor days stretched from 24 to 46 days in FY26—and you collect ₹12.10 in Cash Flow from Operations (₹128 crore). Then subtract ₹16.54 of capital expenditure (₹175 crore) for MF3, MF4, and MF5, and you end FY26 with negative ₹4.44 of Free Cash Flow (-₹47 crore).

And look at the supply-chain tension sitting behind that working-capital line. Over 70% of SEDEMAC's raw material cost is tied to semiconductors and imported electronic components, including PCBs from China. In H1 FY27, as global chip lead times tightened again, management deliberately shortened its payable days—paying suppliers faster to secure wafer and component allocations—while building inventory buffers. Working capital nearly doubled from ₹135 crore in March 2026 to ₹258 crore by September 2026. The unit economics at the factory gate are stellar, but the cash conversion cycle is hostage to silicon supply chains and OEM payment terms.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The ₹100 waterfall exposes the central paradox of SEDEMAC's business model: software-grade gross/EBITDA margins (20.5% OPM) paired with hardware-grade capital intensity (106–120 inventory days and ₹175 crore of FY26 capex). Until MF3 ramps and semiconductor lead times normalize, accounting profits will outpace free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Inside the Chakan-to-Shoolagiri Manufacturing Build-Out
paragraphs: Walk through why SEDEMAC's capital intensity stepped up so sharply between FY25 and H1 FY27. Electronics manufacturing for automotive OEMs is not a garage operation; it requires high-speed automated surface-mount technology (SMT) lines, conformal coating for moisture and vibration protection, automated optical inspection, and 100% end-of-line functional test rigs. When MF1 in Chakan crossed 90% utilization, SEDEMAC could not simply outsource overflow to a generic contract manufacturer without risking automotive quality certifications and IP leakage.

Instead, management chose to triple its Chakan footprint with MF3—120,000 square feet that entered pilot production in Q2 FY27—while carving out MF4 (9,000 square feet) for electric machines and securing 13 acres at Shoolagiri in Tamil Nadu for MF5. Positioning MF5 in Tamil Nadu is a deliberate supply-chain move: it places automated ECU and motor-controller lines within trucking distance of South Indian two-wheeler and EV assembly plants, cutting freight friction and deepening OEM integration. The trade-off, as the FY26 waterfall proved, is ₹175 crore of capex and negative ₹47 crore of Free Cash Flow during the build phase.
